A caller-backed finish converges and prints the Plan Dispatcher export hint when the model's final review says source review is incomplete and lists no planning gap. The cost is small: one term in the line-981 predicate (caller-backed runs need coverage.source_review_status == 'complete'), a specific next_action, and a strict list-of-strings check for planning_gaps at line 961, matching review_problems lines 719-721. In the cohort it changes 0 of 9 live outcomes: it costs no new stops and has no measured gain, because every incomplete review there also listed a gap. So treat it as a cheap safeguard and bundle it with the next Backchain change rather than giving it its own release. Two scope limits: do not gate on material findings (finding lists include ones already repaired), and amend references/convergence.md lines 201-204, which today describes exactly what the code does.

groups.value_reason:
Adopt, with a narrower scope than Astra proposes. Each reproduction holds, and the export-gate bypass is real: a single added initial_state string marks an incomplete inherited plan complete and lets the run converge. Earlier research names this exact model failure ('Silent inv-7 repair'; backchain b17826c). The fix is a few lines next to the existing preservation errors.

1. Goal and origin, legacy mode: make goal equality and inherited-step origin equality errors in inherited_obligations. Cost is zero on the evidence: 0 of 30 inherited cohort runs changed either.
2. initial_state: do not require it unchanged. Report every added or removed fact as a review difference, and make it an error only when an added fact covers an inherited goal_needs entry or an inherited null-edge need that the inherited plan left open. Strict equality would have refused 6 of 15 control runs whose inspection-derived additions all three graders accepted, and it contradicts the convergence review's 'evidenced initial fact' route.
3. Edge keys: confirmed but adversarial-only (no real ID contains '<-' or is 'null'). The cheap fix is one prepare-time refusal: when edit_bounds are present, refuse with exit 3 if any inherited step ID contains '<-' or equals 'null'. That leaves the general ID schema alone and avoids a typed-identity refactor that measured gain does not justify.

Under the KISS and measured-gain rules, items 1-2 are worth it because the bypass silently completes a plan; item 3 is a guard plus a contract note.

groups.risks_and_interactions:
Risks:
- Overreach on initial_state. A strict equality rule would stop inherited runs, including ShipLoop replans through the draft or caller route, whose honest repair adds an inspected fact. That is a ShipLoop stop-behaviour trade-off, so ask the owner before adopting strict equality. The narrow goal-need or null-edge rule avoids it.
- Source-aware extension. If initial_state checks reach bound_errors, they must allow adding a caller's protected accepted fact (b655b804 lines 308-318), or the pilot regression returns in reverse.
- Fresh route stays uncovered. Its direct draft authors initial_state, and the draft→plan freeze comparison and the per-cycle baseline compare only goal_needs and confirmations, so an invented fact in a fresh draft stays a semantic-review issue. Say so in convergence.md's table (lines 94-99), which documents the mechanical scope.

Interactions:
- Plan Dispatcher export: `export PLAN` (export_graph 348-391) never consults run preservation, so this fix does not stop exporting a hand-edited plan. That is recommendation 7's run-aware export route; the two should land together or at least be cross-referenced.
- Release gate: a backchain-only change needs changes/backchain/<slug>.md. It does not touch skills/shiploop, so the ShipLoop E2E preflight is not triggered unless ShipLoop's plan packet text changes.
- Rubric-eval and cohort comparability: the candidate arm never changed goal, origin or initial_state (0/15), so earlier candidate verdicts stay comparable. The cohort's only mechanical oracle for this is plan-fields-unchanged (revenue-export-lineage; 0 failures in 60 runs). The semantic criteria accepted control-arm fact additions, so a strict rule would redefine 'correct' against earlier evidence. Record that in the journal if strict equality is ever chosen.
- Edge keys: caller-contract.md line 147 defines the string key format. Any change to how keys are resolved, or a refusal of odd IDs, must update that text, and ShipLoop or any other caller packet producer must not emit IDs containing '<-' or 'null'.

claims.claim: Astra's suggested wording ('a discovered supplier may establish a shared subset ... when the seed consumes it, retains substantive remaining work and its original acceptance obligations, and ... each implementation task exactly one owner') permits the extraction without opening a loophole.
claims.evidence: The wording does block duplicated implementation (one owner) and keeps the seed's confirmation (the seed consumes the supplier and retains its acceptance obligations). It has no trigger, though. Applied to eval 22's legacy-edge-free fixture, which has no consumer at all, it would allow D=schema, S1<-D, with S1 keeping purge as 'substantive remaining work'. That turns eval 22's expected 'blocked' into a permitted split, so legacy mode would gain a general license to split chunks. 'Substantive' is undefined. The wording also does not require the extracted supplier to have its own exact confirmation, or the consumer to end up with no path to the seed. A safer form ties the exception to a consumer-driven dependency defect. Proposed text: 'Exception, consumer-driven shared supplier: when another step needs only one conjunct of an inherited seed's produce and has no inherited edge to that seed, a discovered step may implement that conjunct if (1) both that consumer and the seed consume it and the consumer gains no path to the seed; (2) the seed keeps its ID, statement, produces, inherited edges and confirmation entries verbatim and still implements at least one other conjunct itself; (3) the supplier produces only the extracted conjunct, has its own confirmation, and no other step implements it; (4) the assessment maps that conjunct to its single implementation owner. A split motivated only by chunk boundaries, a consumer that still waits on the seed through an inherited edge, or a seed left with only verification remains narrowing.' Under this text, eval 20 (inherited edge to the seed) and eval 22 (no consumer) stay blocked, and orders-cancel-rpc's store extraction becomes permitted.

claims.claim: (b) cohort.py grader_noise and the rubric-eval SPEC section 8 near-identical band are repeat-grading noise divided by sqrt(passes), which is not an acceptable-loss margin. Better graders shrink the band and make adoption harder.
claims.evidence:
Formula. cohort.py grader_noise (line 1539, measured/sqrt(passes) at line 1549), uncommitted because backchain .gitignore ignores results/. rubric_eval.py pass_noise (line 362), with analyze dividing it by passes**0.5 at lines 625-630, falling back to judge_noise. The band test is rubric_eval.py:547 in decide (line 512) and cohort.py:1477 in decide (line 1450). SPEC section 7 lines 174-176 says the noise 'is the smallest difference this judge can tell apart, and analyze uses it as the equivalence bound', and lines 194-198 give the divide-by-sqrt rule. Section 8 lines 260-263: 'a difference smaller than the judge's own test-retest change is not material'. Nothing in the SPEC, SKILL.md or rubric_eval.py mentions a margin or acceptable loss. The only override is scripts/rubric-eval line 58, --noise, set at analyze time and not pre-registered. PROTOCOL.md line 8 asks whether the candidate plans 'at least as well as' the control, a non-inferiority question, but its rule (line 102) uses the noise band.

Direction, with the cohort's own numbers. analysis.json: raw pass difference 1.819, band 1.05, quality interval [-8.85, +6.26]. Calling cohort.decide on the real paired dicts gives inconclusive for noise 0, 0.62, 1.05 and 5.0. At noise 8.85 or above (a raw pass difference of 15.3 or more, about 8.4 times noisier than measured) it returns winner=candidate decided_by=tokens, unblocked, even though bounded-source-edge-repair lost 26.6 points per case. R1 (the regrade): band 0.62, interval [-1.93, +7.49]; noise of 7.49 or more flips it to a token win. rubric_eval.decide behaves the same: ship=True at 8.85, inconclusive at 8.84. The R1 regrade is a real instance of a better grader shrinking the band (raw 1.82 to 1.07; bound 1.05 to 0.62). Guardrail tolerance (rubric_eval.py:540-541, SPEC lines 276-278) also scales with noise. In a probe, a guardrail mean of -3.0 blocked at noise 0.62 and 1.05 but shipped at 3.5.

Simulation (10 cases, 3 reps, 3 passes, case SD 1.5, with grader noise also widening the interval): with a true -2 point loss, P(near-identical, so cost decides) is 0.00 for grader SD 0.5 and 2, 0.34 for SD 5 and 0.83 for SD 10. Fixed-comparison probe: C(-1, -3, +1, p=0.5) with fewer tokens has ship=False at noise 0.6 and 2.0, and ship=True at 3.5.

claims.claim: (c) Requiring the bootstrap and the Wilcoxon test to agree is conservative, not a correctness check.
claims.evidence:
How decide combines the tests. A material better or worse result goes through significant() (rubric_eval.py lines 491-497; cohort.py lines 1424-1431). It needs three things: Wilcoxon p<0.05 (two-sided; the statistic's own sign is never read), the 95% interval excluding zero on that side, and the scenario/case mean on the same side. A cost win goes through the same function (_efficiency, line 500). Near-identical uses the bootstrap interval alone (line 547), and harms block on the interval alone (lines 538-541; cohort.py lines 1459-1462). wilcoxon() returns None when fewer than 6 case means are non-zero (rubric_eval.py lines 393-394), and then nothing can be significant. That already happens to the cohort's qualified measure, where p=None.

Simulation (n=10 clusters, 3 reps, rubric_eval.bootstrap and wilcoxon). Under the null, false positives were: bootstrap alone 10.3%, Wilcoxon 5.0%, conjunction 4.7%. Power at shift 5: 32% / 20.3% / 20.3%. At shift 10: 75.7% / 60.7% / 60.3%. So the conjunction behaves almost exactly like the Wilcoxon test with a mean-sign check; it is conservative.

Nuance against Astra: the SPEC never presents the rule as a correctness check. It calls it 'stricter' (section 8, lines 312-315) and justifies it because 'a percentile bootstrap over few clusters runs narrow' (lines 255-256). The simulation confirms the rationale: about 2x nominal false positives at 10 clusters. The two tests do answer different questions (mean of cells vs location of case means), so Astra's call for one primary estimand stands. The current rule is a defensible safeguard for the bootstrap, not an error. The rule came from c7f78d95f72b49e633b7092316fcf027adc62607 (adversarial-review fix, 2026-09-27).

groups.value_reason:
Worth doing. The defect is real, it can be reproduced on the released code, and it points the wrong way: a noisier judge widens the near-identical band. A possible 3-point loss with fewer tokens ships at noise 3.5 and not at 0.6. With this cohort's own interval, any band of 8.85 or more ships the candidate on tokens. In simulation, a true 2-point loss is declared near-identical 83% of the time with judge SD 10, and never with SD 2. At the same time, at practical sizes the cost-decides path is unreachable: about 518 cases would be needed. Neither failure appears in any current report.

Concrete changes:

(1) Owner-set, pre-registered acceptable-loss margin, delta in points.
- Store it in the round manifest when `build` writes it, with the owner and date; a suite default in rubric.json may supply it. analyze reads it from the manifest. The `--noise` CLI flag (scripts/rubric-eval line 58) stays a measurement override and can never set the margin. The tool never chooses delta; a missing margin is a blocker in decide, like the unmeasured-noise blocker at rubric_eval.py lines 530-531.
- Shape it as non-inferiority, to match PROTOCOL 'at least as well as': cost decides when low >= -delta. Today C(+2, -0.5, +5) with fewer tokens is inconclusive.

(2) Noise as a floor, meaning a precondition, not a widening. When the measured noise/sqrt(passes) exceeds delta, decide blocks with 'judge cannot resolve the margin'. Widening to max(delta, noise) would bring the inverted direction back. The guardrail check `mean < -noise` (lines 540-541) gets the same treatment.

(3) Precision/power report. analyze reports the interval half-width against delta and the projected cases, N*(half-width/delta)^2. Pre-registration states the projected cases from pilot between-case SD. This would have flagged before running that ~518 cases were needed for band 1.05, or about 55 for delta=2 at R1's 4.71 half-width.

(4) Critical defects as their own outcome. Criteria may carry `critical: true`, as the cohort's cases.json already does. analyze counts outputs with a critical criterion missed by a majority of passes, compares them paired, and blocks on a rise (harm blocks on the interval alone, as now).

(5) Cost by token class. model_call.py records uncached input, cache read, cache write, output and reasoning separately (lines 117-120, 159-161, 233-234). usage() (lines 583-590) and analyze report each class plus the total. The decision measure stays the pre-registered total.

SPEC sections:
- Section 7: rewrite lines 174-176 and 194-198 so noise is measurement resolution, not the equivalence bound.
- Section 8: decision steps 1-3 at lines 258-270; blocking checks at lines 272-291 (add the margin-missing, noise-exceeds-margin and critical-rise blocks); token-use paragraph at lines 247-251; keep lines 253-256 and 309-315 but name one primary estimand.

groups.risks_and_interactions:
Comparability. Earlier ship decisions were made under the noise band: rubric-eval rounds 3-6, the prune3 and design v2 decisions in SPEC section 7, and this cohort's protocol. Re-analysing them under delta can flip some; record flips the way SPEC section 7 records judge changes, and ask the owner before switching, because it is a default that breaks comparability.

Margin abuse. A wide 'convenience' delta is not evidence. Pre-register it in the manifest with a hash, refuse analyze-time changes, and keep `--noise` from acting as a back door; today it lets an analyst set any band after seeing results.

Budget. With between-case SD of 8-13 points, a 2-3 point margin needs about 25-55 cases at roughly 1M tokens per attempt and 6 attempts per case. The precision report will often say 'unreachable at this size'. That outcome is honest, and the owner may then choose an explicit decision under uncertainty, labelled as such.

Two implementations. cohort.py duplicates decide and grader_noise, and it is uncommitted (backchain .gitignore ignores results/). Fix both together or have the cohort import rubric_eval; commit the runner as Astra recommends.

ShipLoop. ShipLoop prompt changes ship through the adversarial-review loop and rubric-eval, so a stricter or different rule changes what clears that gate. Rounds in flight should finish under the old rule and say so.

Plan Dispatcher export. No interaction.

Release gate. Needs a changes/rubric-eval/*.md note, plus a test/rubric-eval.test.py update in the same commit. It does not touch skills/shiploop, so no E2E preflight applies.

Bootstrap and Wilcoxon. If a single primary estimand replaces the AND rule, keep a small-cluster correction: the percentile bootstrap alone produced 10.3% false positives at 10 clusters, so dropping the Wilcoxon outright would double false ships.

Critical-defect block. It can fire on grader artifacts, such as the parallel_groups confusion that R1 corrected (8 to 5 candidate critical misses). Calibrate the critical criteria first.

Token-class reporting. It shows the uncached saving is relatively smaller (-27.6%) than the headline (-48.5%). Any cost-weighted figure needs the owner's price table; the tool must not assume one.
